tasks.short: Negotiate major agreements and approve commitments within delegated authority.

steps.what: Collect the commercial brief, existing agreement, performance history and approval limits.
Compare proposed terms with approved positions and identify material departures.

loop.input: Proposed agreement, existing agreement and approved clause positions.
loop.output: Clause-linked departures, missing terms and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Check clause references and numeric terms; legal team validates material interpretations.
loop.stop: One comparison and one repair pass; missing text or unresolved interpretation goes to legal team.
loop.why_not_simpler: Rules can compare amounts and dates, but negotiated wording changes obligations.

steps.what: Set acceptable trade-offs, concessions and escalation limits.
Negotiate price, obligations and concessions with the counterparty.
Validate final wording and obtain the required commercial approval.
Execute the approved agreement with the counterparty.
File the signed agreement and record obligations, owners and renewal dates.

tasks.design: Connect {PROCUREMENT}, {ERP} and {CLM} to assemble the agreement pack, then use a bounded model comparison to draft clause-linked departures. Configure approval routing in {CLM} and execution in {ESIGN}, with human decisions on concessions, final terms and signature; approved metadata feeds renewal reminders.
tasks.previous_blocker: Agreements and commercial history were scattered. Reliable comparison of varied wording needed substantial legal effort.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing approval and signature features cover much of the flow. AI-assisted coding reduces connector work, and bounded text comparison can prepare a reviewable first pass.
tasks.still_hard: Novel liability, bargaining leverage, enforceability and counterparty intent require expertise. Poor scans and bespoke agreements increase review costs.
tasks.human_edge: Read the counterparty, trade concessions and accept responsibility for commitments.

ambition.what: Monthly review of upcoming renewals with material supplier concentration.

tasks.altitude: Less time goes into assembling papers and chasing approvals; more goes into negotiation preparation and renewal choices. Existing signing and board approval rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Validate service obligations before contract approval.
reach.learn: Translate negotiated promises into operating capacity, service measures and accountable owners.

evidence.claim: Approval routing, signature preparation and contract metadata handling can use configured workflows.
Bounded clause comparison can assist legal review; the digest supplies no documented contract-negotiation case.

assumptions: Time shares describe a representative major supplier agreement and are estimates, not measurements.
The approval matrix distinguishes commercial approval from legal execution.
An approved obligation schedule supplies structured metadata for filing.
Build ranges are working effort for one agreement family and a limited rollout.
Confidential agreements require access controls and GDPR-compliant handling of personal data.
unknowns: Which agreement families reach the chief executive?
Which commitments require board approval or more than one signatory?
Are approved clause positions and obligation schedules maintained?
research_questions: How accurately can clause departures be identified across representative agreement formats?
Which existing configuration covers approval routing and renewal reminders?
new_work: Validate material clause departures and handle unsupported formats.
Maintain approved positions, approval limits and signatory permissions.
Check connector failures and agreement-version integrity.

tasks.short: Define departmental responsibilities and resolve coordination problems across functions and sites.

steps.what: Gather current responsibilities, recurring handoff problems and site constraints.
Draft responsibility changes and identify overlapping ownership or missing handoffs.

loop.input: Current responsibility matrix and submitted handoff issues.
loop.output: Proposed matrix with source-linked conflicts and unresolved ownership questions.
loop.check: Validate department names and required owners; operations manager checks inferred conflicts.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; disputed ownership remains explicitly unresolved.
loop.why_not_simpler: Missing owners can be checked by rules, but informal responsibilities arrive as narrative descriptions.

steps.what: Resolve competing priorities and negotiate responsibilities with department and site leaders.
Check employee impacts and complete consultation required by national rules.
Approve responsibilities, escalation paths and the effective date.
Publish approved responsibilities and assign implementation actions.
Review unresolved handoffs and escalate implementation failures.

tasks.design: Configure structured issue intake and responsibility records in {PROJECT}, linked to approved organization records in {HCM}. A bounded model drafts changes from submitted evidence; leaders resolve ownership and complete applicable consultation before approval releases publication and implementation actions through {DOCS} and {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Responsibility documents drifted from actual practice. Much of the relevant knowledge lived in conversations and separate departmental records.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured forms and versioned records can replace mailbox consolidation. A small model loop can organize narrative issues without deciding who should hold power.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting incentives, informal influence and resource shortages do not disappear with a clearer matrix. Employee consultation can determine the implementation timetable.
tasks.human_edge: Broker workable compromises and judge whether authority, resources and accountability actually match.

ambition.what: Quarterly cross-site handoff clinic for unresolved ownership disputes.

tasks.altitude: The chief executive spends less time reconstructing responsibilities and more time settling the few conflicts that need executive authority. The operations manager can gain explicit authority to resolve routine handoff disputes if the chief executive delegates it.

reach.learn: Map dependencies, test capacity constraints and define escalation thresholds.

evidence.claim: Structured responsibility records, issue intake and publication can use configured records and workflow features.
Narrative handoff issues can support a bounded drafting loop, while responsibility decisions remain human.

assumptions: Time shares are estimates for a change affecting several departments or sites.
Minor coordination changes may need only an employee impact check; formal consultation depends on national rules.
The initial scope covers departmental responsibilities.
Employee-level decision support requires assessment under GDPR, the EU AI Act and national rules.
Publication uses the approved version and effective date.
Build ranges cover working effort; consultation can add elapsed waiting time.
unknowns: Which national rules and employee representation arrangements apply?
Who currently maintains the responsibility matrix?
Can {PROJECT}, {HCM} and {DOCS} share approved records through supported interfaces?
research_questions: Can existing record and form features represent responsibility ownership without custom software?
How often do narrative issue summaries omit a material dependency?
new_work: Review inferred ownership conflicts and unresolved questions.
Maintain responsibility versions, department identifiers and access permissions.
Check implementation outcomes and keep consultation records current.

tasks.short: Prepare and deliver speeches, articles and presentations that advance organizational objectives.

steps.what: Choose the audience, purpose and message with the communications team.
Collect approved figures, examples and source material.
Draft the speech, article or presentation and likely audience questions.

loop.input: Communication brief, approved source pack, format limits and voice guidance.
loop.output: Draft content and likely questions with references for factual claims.
loop.check: Verify numbers and source references; communications team checks claims, tone and unsupported promises.
loop.stop: One draft and two revisions within the requested length; unsupported claims are removed or escalated.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates structure the output, but audience-specific prose and transitions require language generation.

steps.what: Review factual claims, disclosures and commitments, then approve the final message.
Rehearse delivery and prepare for difficult questions.
Deliver the presentation and respond to audience questions.
Publish approved material and record audience questions for follow-up.

tasks.design: Generate a source pack from approved material in {DOCS} and figures in {BI}, then use a bounded model loop to prepare a speech, article or presentation. Human editorial approval controls the message and publication through {CMS}; {PROJECT} holds audience follow-up actions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Preparation required repeated searches, manual adaptation and several writing passes. Generic templates did little for voice or audience fit.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded drafting can turn approved source material into a useful first version. Deterministic source and number checks make review more focused.
tasks.still_hard: Personal voice, sensitive disclosures and spontaneous questions remain demanding. A polished draft can still contain unsupported claims.
tasks.human_edge: Choose what the organization should stand behind, earn audience trust and answer under pressure.

ambition.what: Monthly review of audience questions to choose future communication topics.

tasks.altitude: Preparation becomes shorter, leaving more time for examples, rehearsal and audience engagement. Editorial responsibility and authority to make public commitments stay with the same people.

reach.task: Provide verified operating examples for executive communication.
reach.learn: Explain operational results clearly and distinguish evidence from aspiration.

evidence.claim: Structured drafting from management documents is an available capability; its use for speeches is an extrapolation.
A government trial reported drafting and presentation time savings, with self-reported results and human oversight.
Public-interest AI-generated text has transparency requirements, with an exception involving human review and editorial responsibility.
A documented report failure included nonexistent references, supporting explicit source verification.

assumptions: Time shares describe a speaking engagement; an article shifts delivery time into writing and review.
The source pack contains material cleared for the intended audience.
The publication workflow records human review and editorial responsibility.
EU AI Act transparency obligations are assessed for the publication context.
GDPR applies to personal stories and other identifiable source material.
Build ranges cover one language and a small set of document formats.
unknowns: Which communication formats and languages recur?
Who approves sensitive disclosures and public commitments?
Are source figures and examples already cleared for publication?
Which interfaces are available in {DOCS}, {BI} and {CMS}?
research_questions: How much editing do drafts need to match the executive's voice?
Can factual claims be traced to approved sources consistently across formats?
new_work: Check source references, factual claims and accidental commitments.
Maintain approved examples, voice guidance and publication permissions.
Review audience questions and assign substantive follow-up.

tasks.short: Maintain relationships and coordinate commitments with shareholders and outside organizations.

steps.what: Collect relationship history, previous commitments and current organizational facts.
Prepare a briefing on interests, outstanding commitments and sensitive topics.

loop.input: Permitted correspondence, recorded commitments, approved figures and meeting agenda.
loop.output: Source-linked briefing separating recorded facts from uncertain interpretations.
loop.check: Verify dates, figures and commitments; executive support checks relevance and access scope.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; conflicting evidence remains flagged for the executive.
loop.why_not_simpler: Interests and sensitivities appear in varied correspondence that fixed fields cannot fully represent.

steps.what: Choose the relationship objective, disclosure limits and possible commitments.
Discuss concerns, build trust and agree next steps with external stakeholders.
Draft the follow-up message and list owners, deadlines and unresolved points.

loop.input: Executive-provided meeting notes, proposed commitments and disclosure limits.
loop.output: Follow-up message and action list with missing owners or dates flagged.
loop.check: Trace commitments to notes; preserve uncertainty and check recipients and disclosure restrictions.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; ambiguous commitments return to the executive.
loop.why_not_simpler: Meeting notes need interpretation and diplomatic wording before they become a usable message.

steps.what: Approve commitments and send the follow-up to the agreed recipients.
Update relationship records and schedule commitment reminders.

tasks.design: Assemble permitted relationship records from {CRM}, {EMAIL} and {DOCS}, then use bounded loops for a source-linked briefing and follow-up draft. The executive conducts the conversation and approves recipients and commitments before sending; approved actions update {PROJECT} and reminders in {CALENDAR}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Relationship context was distributed across personal correspondence and informal notes. Administrative tools could track contacts but could not reliably prepare nuanced briefs.
tasks.enabler_now: Small integrations can gather permitted records, while bounded drafting can organize correspondence and meeting notes. Existing task and calendar features handle reminders.
tasks.still_hard: Trust, conflicting stakeholder interests and selective disclosure remain personal judgments. Incomplete notes can misstate what was actually agreed.
tasks.human_edge: Sense unspoken concerns, handle disagreement and make credible commitments within organizational authority.
tasks.altitude: The executive arrives better prepared and spends less time reconstructing commitments afterward. More time is available for difficult relationships; decision rights do not change.

reach.task: Deliver operational commitments made to external stakeholders.
reach.learn: Test feasibility, negotiate realistic deadlines and escalate delivery risks before promises are made.

evidence.claim: Briefing and follow-up drafting can use bounded source-based loops, but the digest provides no stakeholder-liaison case.
The government trial supports possible drafting savings, with self-reported results and required human oversight.
Approved action lists can feed configured records, task assignment and calendar reminders.

assumptions: Time shares are estimates for a substantive external stakeholder meeting.
Meeting notes are provided by participants; recording is not required.
Only correspondence explicitly within the authorized access scope is retrieved.
GDPR applies to stakeholder records, retention and access.
Drafting assistance receives an EU AI Act assessment appropriate to its intended use.
Build ranges cover one relationship register and a limited mailbox access scope.
unknowns: Where are shareholder and external relationship records held?
Which correspondence may executive support access?
Which commitments need legal, finance or board approval?
Who owns action completion and stakeholder-record retention?
Do national rules require consultation for the proposed mailbox access arrangements?
research_questions: How reliably do briefing drafts distinguish recorded facts from inferred stakeholder interests?
Can commitments be transferred into existing task records without duplicate entry?
new_work: Review briefing interpretations and ambiguous commitments.
Maintain access scopes, retention settings and relationship records.
Handle overdue actions and reconcile commitments changed after meetings.

role.altitude: The chief executive spends less time assembling context, drafting routine material and chasing follow-through. Negotiation, organizational trade-offs, public commitments and relationship work remain central; additional decision rights require explicit delegation.
reach: General and operations manager: turn executive commitments into feasible delivery plans.
Legal team: translate commercial intent into enforceable terms and clear approval limits.
Communications team: build evidence-backed messages and maintain editorial accountability.
skills_to_grow: Define decision limits and distinguish preparation from authorization.
Review source-linked drafts and spot unsupported claims or commitments.
Translate strategy into clear responsibilities and measurable handoffs.
Understand access controls, GDPR obligations and applicable national consultation rules.
role.ambitious_version: Use dependable preparation and commitment records to identify cross-functional conflicts earlier, then delegate routine resolution to the general and operations manager within explicit limits.
